rationale: Direct evidence from recent peer-reviewed investigations and clinical gene curation databases demonstrates that pathogenic variants in RAB3A (the gene underlying SCA52) generate an expanded clinical spectrum spanning from pure cerebellar ataxia to hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP) phenotypes. Mouraux et al. (2025) identified pathogenic RAB3A variants in spastic paraplegia cohorts (frequency 0.81%), documenting that ataxia may be co-expressed with pyramidal signs such as spasticity and hyperreflexia, notably in association with variants like p.Asp83Trp. OMIM entry #621535 and national gene panels (e.g., Genomics England PanelApp) have formally integrated hereditary spastic paraplegia into the RAB3A/SCA52 disease spectrum. Therefore, prominent pyramidal signs and spasticity do not rule out SCA52.

evidence.text: Mouraux et al. identify RAB3A variants in hereditary spastic paraplegia patients at a frequency of 0.81%, establishing that RAB3A variants cause a phenotypic continuum from cerebellar ataxia to spastic paraplegia and that pyramidal signs accompany cerebellar ataxia in individuals with specific mutations like p.Asp83Trp.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact genotype-phenotype correlation across distinct RAB3A functional domains (e.g., GTP-binding pocket versus effector interface) in determining pure ataxia versus predominant spastic paraplegia?
new_directions.rationale: Mouraux et al. noted that pyramidal signs are associated with the common p.Asp83Trp mutation, whereas other variants may alter vesicle release dynamics differently. Systematic biophysical and cohort analysis could clarify variant-specific manifestation risk.

new_directions.question_text: What is the longitudinal trajectory and onset age of corticospinal tract signs in RAB3A variant carriers presenting initially with congenital or infantile-onset cerebellar ataxia?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether spastic paraparesis is an age-dependent, progressive development in SCA52 or a distinct presentation will improve diagnostic stratification.
